script: Hitler was outsmarted by a group of artists and inflatable balloons. During World War Two, the Allies needed to move thousands of troops across the Rhine, but they were badly outnumbered. One wrong move meant a massacre. The solution? Recruit artists, actors, and architects to build a fake army out of rubber, canvas, and plywood. From the air, these inflatable tanks looked terrifyingly real. Massive speakers blasted recordings of fake troop movements for miles. They tricked the Nazis into thinking a huge force was attacking, while the real army moved completely undetected. Patton didn't win by force alone. He won with a masterclass in deception.
